items.title: comments.divider_width config key
items.action: Add the `comments` section with `divider_width` (default 88, a positive integer) in the four places: `defaults.json`; `harness.schema.json` (an object, additionalProperties false, divider_width an integer with minimum 1, described as read by the writing-comments section command); `config.py` (a frozen `CommentsConfig` dataclass beside `DocstringsConfig`, a `comments: CommentsConfig` field on `HarnessConfig`, a `_comments()` builder mirroring `_docstrings()` with its own unknown-key and positive-integer checks so a load without jsonschema refuses with a message starting `comments`, wired into the one `HarnessConfig(...)` call); and a README key-table row after `docstrings.line_length`.

items.title: Section checker: models, API, comment_sections.py and its root-separation case
items.action: `writing_comments_models.py`: `DividerLevel` (major, minor), `FlagKind` (width, style, banner), closed pydantic models `Divider(line, level, title)`, `CommentFlag(line, kind, text)` and `SectionReport(dividers, flags)`. `writing_comments_api.py`: `sections(source, width)` reads full-line comments through `tokenize` (so docstring underlines and trailing comments never count; a tokenize error raises ValueError); a rule is `# ` plus dashes only; a major divider is a rule, a title comment, any further comment lines, then a closing rule at the same indent, reported at its first rule; a minor divider matches `# -- <title> ----`; a rule outside a complete banner is a banner flag; any other full-line comment holding a run of 4 or more of `-=*~_#` is a style flag; each rule and minor line whose length (indentation included) is not the width is a width flag. `rule_line(indent, width)`, `minor_line(title, indent, width)` build the canonical lines; `report_lines(label, report)` prints `<label>:<n>: major|minor <title>` and `<label>:<n>: flag <kind>: <text>` in line order, or `<label>: no dividers`. `skills/writing-comments/commands/comment_sections.py <path>...`: activates the project config (width from `comments.divider_width`), labels each file relative to the project, prints the files in the order named; a missing path, a non-`.py` file, an unparsable file or no path is a `problem:` line on stderr, exit 1, nothing on stdout. Add the `comment-sections` case to `CASES` and `MUST_EXIT_ZERO` in test_root_separation.py.

items.title: writing-comments skill through the strap gate
items.action: Run `harness:strap-skills writing-comments` end to end (new, classify, check, red, scaffold, draw, baselines, write, greens, freeze). The checker's code is proven by TASK-2's tests; the spec lists `comment_sections.py` and `comment_format.md` with `add_part` (scaffold keeps the existing models and API modules), and its mechanical behaviors are contract-test pins only: the SKILL.md frontmatter `Use when` trigger and the command run through hpy. Judgment behaviors to classify and strap: (1) a process comment states what the code cannot show (a constraint, an ordering, an invariant, why one branch wins) in one line where it fits, never restates the next line, carries no review, PR or plan citation, and uses third person; (2) dividers go into a module the work creates once it holds more than one group of definitions, or on an explicit ask; an untouched module, or an untouched block's non-canonical divider, stays as it is under `while you are in there` pressure (D4); (3) a section pass runs comment_sections.py, uses major dividers for top-level groups and minor ones inside them, and clears every flag in the blocks it writes. `comment_format.md` states both canonical forms (D2), the width key (D3) and the process-comment rules with the issue's examples.

the two plus `### ===== NAME ===== ###` as a class-group level
